page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage, requiring network-attached storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates solid compute capabilities, achieving a stress-ng single-core score of 1435.39 and a multi-core score of 30631.79. The memory subsystem delivers a read-only small-block cached bandwidth of 1704.01 GB/sec, which drops to 104.96 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES, contributing to a Passmark CPU score of 29137.73 and a Redis SET performance of 29.05 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfc6.8xlarge is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2:1 and the complete absence of bundled local storage. This design prioritizes raw CPU execution over memory-intensive caching or high-capacity local disk operations, making it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The instance is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, web serving, and moderate-scale parallel processing workloads.
